title: Recruiters are using AI avatars to run interviews. Now candidates are sending avatars to attend them.
excerpt: A Sydney recruiter disqualified three applicants who appeared as AI avatars. Gartner expects one in four candidate profiles to be fake by 2028.
content_html:
Job recruiters are meeting an uncanny new kind of candidate: the AI avatar. These digital humans mirror an applicant’s voice and likeness while being something else entirely, and they are turning up in first-round interviews.

Lana Kersanava, a Sydney-based recruiter, told Semafor she has encountered them over the past six months. “At the beginning, it’s like you feel like something is off,” she said, adding: “It looks very realistic.”

How she spotted it

The tell was not the rendering, which held up. It was the answers, delivered with a polish that never faltered across a run of questions.

After roughly five minutes, Kersanava ended the interview and disqualified the candidate. She has now done this three times.

The detail worth pausing on

All three avatar candidates had applied for English-speaking roles as non-native speakers, leaning on the technology to cover a gap in language proficiency. That is a different proposition from someone faking a work history.

It also lands in a hiring market with a documented bias problem. Research has found recruiters up to 19% less likely to follow up with job seekers from immigrant and ethnic minority backgrounds than with equally qualified candidates.

None of which makes an undisclosed avatar acceptable. It does complicate the framing of these candidates as straightforward fraudsters.

The system they are responding to

Applicant tracking systems already use AI to filter CVs before a human reads them, and recruiters increasingly deploy AI avatars to conduct first-round interviews themselves. Candidates are now answering machines with machines.

The resulting AI-on-AI war is rewriting the hiring playbook, pushing employers towards live technical walk-throughs, scenario challenges, and roleplay simulations that are harder to automate through.

The volumes explain the arms race. Nearly two-thirds of candidates now use AI in applications and 87% of US hiring managers use it in hiring, alongside a 239% surge in AI-generated applications.

How common this is

A 2026 Greenhouse report found 91% of US hiring managers have encountered or suspected AI-generated answers during online interviews. Across 19,368 live interviews analysed between July 2025 and January 2026, 38.5% of candidates were flagged for AI-assisted behaviour.

The trajectory points one way. Gartner projects that by 2028 one in four job candidate profiles globally will be fake, spanning AI-generated profiles, deepfake video interviews, and fabricated work histories.

Barriers to entry are minimal. Palo Alto Networks found it takes as little as 70 minutes for someone with no image manipulation experience to build a fake candidate capable of passing a video interview.

Employers are retreating to the room

Seventy-two per cent of recruiting leaders now run at least one in-person stage specifically to counter AI-assisted fraud, with Google, McKinsey, and Cisco reintroducing mandatory face-to-face rounds.

That solves detection at the cost of everything remote hiring was meant to deliver. Candidates who cannot travel, including many of the international applicants this technology most tempts, lose access first.

The screening was never that good

There is an awkward premise underneath the panic, which is that the automated filtering being defended works. The case against AI CV screening has been made repeatedly and forcefully, largely on the grounds that it optimises for keyword matching rather than capability.

Candidates optimising against that filter with better tools is a predictable outcome rather than a moral collapse. Kersanava’s five-minute detection rate also suggests the current generation of avatars is not fooling attentive humans.

What it is doing is making the first round worthless for everyone. If the machine screens the machine, the interview stops measuring anything, which is an argument for changing the process rather than policing the candidates.

content_html_zh:
招聘人员正在遇到一种不可思议的新型候选人：人工智能化身。 这些数字人反映了申请人的声音和肖像，但又完全不同，他们出现在第一轮面试中。

悉尼招聘人员拉娜·克萨纳瓦 (Lana Kersanava) 告诉 Semafor，她在过去六个月里遇到过这些人。 “一开始，你会觉得有些不对劲，”她说，并补充道：“这看起来非常现实。”

她是如何发现的

说明的不是渲染，它是成立的。 这就是答案，经过精心修饰，在面对一系列问题时从未动摇过。

大约五分钟后，克萨纳瓦结束了面试并取消了该候选人的资格。 现在她已经这样做了三次。

值得暂停的细节

所有三名虚拟化身候选人都以非母语者的身份申请了英语角色，依靠技术来弥补语言能力的差距。 这与伪造工作经历的人的主张不同。

它还进入了一个存在偏见问题的招聘市场。 研究发现，与同等资格的候选人相比，招聘人员跟进移民和少数族裔背景求职者的可能性要低 19%。

这些都不能让未公开的化身被接受。 这确实使这些候选人被定性为彻头彻尾的欺诈者变得更加复杂。

他们正在响应的系统

申请人跟踪系统已经使用人工智能在人类阅读简历之前对其进行过滤，并且招聘人员越来越多地部署人工智能化身来自行进行第一轮面试。 候选人现在正在用机器答录机。

由此产生的人工智能对人工智能的战争正在改写招聘手册，推动雇主进行现场技术演练、场景挑战和角色扮演模拟，这些都很难自动化完成。

这些书解释了军备竞赛。 现在，近三分之二的候选人在应用程序中使用人工智能，87% 的美国招聘经理在招聘中使用人工智能，同时人工智能生成的应用程序激增 239%。

这有多常见

2026 年 Greenhouse 报告发现，91% 的美国招聘经理在在线面试中遇到或怀疑过人工智能生成的答案。 在 2025 年 7 月至 2026 年 1 月期间分析的 19,368 次现场面试中，38.5% 的候选人被标记为人工智能辅助行为。

轨迹指向一个方向。 Gartner 预计，到 2028 年，全球四分之一的求职者资料将是虚假的，包括人工智能生成的资料、深度伪造的视频面试和捏造的工作经历。

进入壁垒很小。 Palo Alto Networks 发现，对于没有图像处理经验的人来说，只需 70 分钟就能构建出能够通过视频面试的虚假候选人。

雇主们正在撤退到房间里

72% 的招聘领导者现在至少进行一次面对面的面试，专门针对人工智能辅助的欺诈行为，谷歌、麦肯锡和思科重新引入了强制性的面对面面试。

这解决了检测问题，但代价是远程招聘本应提供的一切。 无法旅行的候选人，包括许多最受这项技术诱惑的国际申请者，首先失去了入学机会。

放映从来没有那么好

恐慌背后有一个尴尬的前提，那就是受到保护的自动过滤是有效的。 反对人工智能简历筛选的理由已经被反复强烈地提出，主要是因为它优化的是关键词匹配而不是能力。

候选人使用更好的工具针对该过滤器进行优化是可预测的结果，而不是道德崩溃。 Kersanava 的五分钟检测率也表明当前一代的化身并没有欺骗细心的人类。

它所做的就是让第一轮对每个人来说都毫无价值。 如果机器对机器进行筛选，面试就会停止衡量任何东西，这是改变流程而不是监管候选人的理由。
